significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that non-equivariant CGCNN/MEGNet-style models contain representations where “symmetry-equivalent atoms receive equivalent embeddings” and that these representations causally support both piezoelectricity and band-degeneracy predictions; this is principally a form-(ii) causal claim, supplemented by form-(i) decodability and a within-orbit/across-orbit ordering. It establishes both a specific phenomenon—differential encoding of inversion, mirror, and rotation symmetries—and a mechanism linking that encoding to two symmetry-governed behavior families, but it does not state a quantitative law predicting encoding strength or performance across models. NequIP (Batzner et al., 2022) and e3nn make equivariance an architectural guarantee, so a verified-false result would still meaningfully rule out emergent symmetry as the operative explanation in the stated non-equivariant model class and favor chemistry-correlated shortcuts or imposed equivariance; true and false therefore denote distinct, informative states. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment to the 5–6 band: replacing these operation-specific and property-specific assertions with the generic topic would leave only the topic’s default representation-plus-causal-probe hypothesis, while the two named behavior families make this particular claim modestly sharper than that median rather than a form-(iii) advance.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the “within-orbit versus across-orbit embedding distance,” decoders for “crystal system, point group, and presence of key symmetry operations,” and the “decoded symmetry direction” used for intervention. These are mainly post-hoc model diagnostics rather than an explicitly claimed forecast, although they could support pre-deployment auditing of whether a trained crystal model has learned the symmetries needed for its target properties. After re-extraction on another CGCNN/MEGNet-style model, the claim predicts a transferable relation—smaller distances for Wyckoff-equivalent sites and selective damage from symmetry-direction ablation—rather than merely prescribing an unconstrained search, and its asserted scope covers a class of graph-based crystal models and multiple symmetry-sensitive tasks. The topic-substitution check supports a score above the median because the generic scientific-representation topic would not itself supply the orbit-distance diagnostic or operation-specific intervention; nevertheless, the claim does not provide a calibrated gating rule or broadly validated forecast for model builders outside this crystal-model family.
